# LP strategy backtesting and fee and IL return estimation — facts

> Source-anchored units about LP strategy backtesting and fee and IL return estimation: 10 across 6 sources. Each line ends in the URL and anchor it came from; `keywords:` names the lexicon terms that matched.

## Structure and components

- [statement] For Base transaction-cost scenarios, the network-fee documentation gives total cost as execution gas times base plus priority fee, plus L1 fee and operator fee. Subtracting only the execution component would omit costs named by the documentation. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-05) — https://docs.base.org/specifications/transactions/network-fees · keywords: LP strategy backtesting and fee and IL return estimation

## How it works

- [statement] For fee estimation, distinguish active liquidity from total deposited capital: a position stops earning swap fees when price leaves its interval. (medium confidence) — https://developers.uniswap.org/docs/get-started/concepts/liquidity-providers/concentrated-liquidity · keywords: LP strategy backtesting and fee and IL return estimation · also: https://blog.uniswap.org/uniswap-v3-math-primer-2
- [statement] The Uniswap math primer derives current position holdings from liquidity, lower and upper ticks, and the pool square-root price. Use its separate in-range and out-of-range formulas when marking a simulated position to market. (low confidence) — https://blog.uniswap.org/uniswap-v3-math-primer-2 · keywords: LP strategy backtesting and fee and IL return estimation

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] In its continuous-time model, the LVR paper decomposes LP returns into market-risk exposure and a microstructure component consisting of accrued fees minus losses to arbitrageurs; fee revenue alone therefore does not describe LP returns. (low confidence) — https://arxiv.org/abs/2208.06046 · keywords: LP strategy backtesting and fee and IL return estimation

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] The open-source Uniswap v3 Active Strategy Framework uses historical swap data for simulations and describes block-level virtual liquidity as an input for approximating fee income. It is a reference implementation, rather than evidence that an arbitrary target pool has been backtested correctly. (low confidence) — https://github.com/ZeroPointLabs/univ3-strategies · keywords: LP strategy backtesting and fee and IL return estimation
- [statement] The framework explicitly warns that it omits gas costs and may suffer Python-versus-Solidity rounding differences and a price feed that differs from the pool price. Treat its simulated results as estimates until these limitations are addressed. (low confidence) — https://github.com/ZeroPointLabs/univ3-strategies · keywords: LP strategy backtesting and fee and IL return estimation
- [statement] Aero documentation distinguishes staked LP positions earning AERO rewards from unstaked LP positions retaining Smart Fees minus an unstaked fee; Smart Fees from the staked positions go to Token Operators. A backtest should model the selected mode rather than crediting both revenue streams to the same position. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-05) — https://aero.xyz/llms-full.txt · keywords: LP strategy backtesting and fee and IL return estimation

## Facts and statements

- [statement] For a fixed-liquidity accounting interval, the Uniswap primer calculates uncollected token fees as position liquidity times the change in inside-range fee growth, divided by the fixed-point scaling factor; pool and tick inputs must refer to the same block. (low confidence) — https://blog.uniswap.org/uniswap-v3-math-primer-2 · keywords: LP strategy backtesting and fee and IL return estimation
- [statement] The RVR authors distinguish impermanent loss, which uses a holding benchmark, from LVR and RVR, which evaluate rebalancing. They caution that efficiently executing a poor asset-management strategy does not make it a good strategy. Report these benchmark comparisons separately. (low confidence) — https://arxiv.org/html/2410.23404v1 · keywords: LP strategy backtesting and fee and IL return estimation
- [statement] The RVR paper scopes its critique of LVR to benchmark realism: the idealized centralized exchange has no fees, spread, or slippage. This does not establish that a concentrated-liquidity bot on Base will outperform holding. (low confidence) — https://arxiv.org/html/2410.23404v1 · keywords: LP strategy backtesting and fee and IL return estimation
